shots.caption: A new agent open on the Build tab with name and Instructions filled in
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Sign in to Copilot Studio.
On the Home page, select the Agent tile. Alternatively, select Agents in the side pane and then New agent. The agent opens in the designer on the Build tab with the name field in focus.
Enter a name for your agent in the name field.
Optionally, use the Agent settings panel to change the primary language, solution, and schema name before you save.
In the Instructions section, describe how the agent should behave, including its role, tone, and any rules it must follow.
Select the Save icon. If you skipped the name, enter it when prompted and select Save.
On the Build tab, confirm that the agent now offers knowledge, tools, skills, connected agents, model, and memory as components you can add next.
instructions: On the Home page, select the Agent tile, or select Agents and then New agent.
Enter a name and write short text in the Instructions section.
Capture the Build tab with the name, Instructions, and the Save icon visible.

shots.caption: The Publish agent dialog with channels listed
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
prerequisites: Preview and test an agent (Microsoft Copilot harness)
setup: Open your agent in Copilot Studio and select Publish.
In the Publish agent dialog, review the agent details and select and configure each channel you want to publish to.
If the dialog says the agent is missing a name, description, or instructions, complete them before you continue.
Select Publish to confirm, and wait for the dialog to show that publishing finished.
When publishing succeeds, use the confirmation to share the agent or add it to the organization catalog.
After you change the agent on the Build tab, select Publish in the upper-right corner, review the Publish your changes dialog, and select Publish to confirm. If publishing fails, select Retry.
instructions: Open an agent that has a name, a description, and instructions.
Select Publish to open the Publish agent dialog.
Capture the dialog with the channel list visible before you confirm.

callouts.note: Review agent details and select the channels to publish to.

callouts.label: Publish
callouts.note: Confirms the publish and starts it.

shots.caption: The Add knowledge dialog on the Build tab
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Open your agent in Copilot Studio and select the Build tab.
In the components panel on the right, select the Knowledge button.

In the Add knowledge dialog, drag and drop files or select the upload area, search for a source, or select a source type such as Public websites, SharePoint, or OneDrive for Business. Use the Advanced tab for more types.
Follow the configuration steps for the source type you selected.
Select Save or Add to confirm the knowledge source.
Update the source name and description so the agent can tell when to use the source.
Select the Preview tab, ask a question the source should answer, and check the activity trace for the knowledge source and its citations.

shots.featureName: Foundry IQ knowledge bases (Microsoft Copilot harness)
shots.caption: The Add a tool dialog with Foundry IQ selected
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Open your agent and select the Build tab.
In the components panel, select Tools to open the Add a tool dialog, and then select Foundry IQ.
Select Create new connection, choose the Authentication type, enter the values it needs, and select Create.
Select Next, select a knowledge base from the list, and select Add to agent. Then select Save.
Select the new Foundry IQ connection under Tools, write a detailed name and description to help orchestration, and select Save.
On the Preview tab, ask a question the knowledge base can answer and open the activity trace to confirm a Foundry IQ retrieval step and the items it returned.
instructions: Open your agent and select the Build tab.

shots.caption: The Add skill dialog with Create from blank
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Open your agent in Copilot Studio and select the Build tab.
In the components panel, select Skills.
In Add skill, select Create from blank.
Enter a Name that uses only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens and does not start or end with a hyphen, such as customer-support-escalation.
Enter a Description that says what the skill does and when it should be activated.
Enter Instructions in Markdown with specific steps, response formats, and constraints, and select Create. The skill appears in the components panel.
Optional: select Skills, then Generate with AI, describe the skill, select Build, answer the questions Copilot asks, and select Add to agent.
Select the Preview tab, send a request that matches the skill purpose, and check the activity trace to confirm the skill ran.
instructions: Open your agent and select the Build tab.
In the components panel, select Skills so Add skill opens.
Capture the dialog with Create from blank visible.

callouts.label: Skills
callouts.note: Components panel button for skills.

callouts.label: Create from blank
callouts.note: Write the name, description, and Markdown instructions yourself.

shots.caption: The Add a tool dialog with the MCP tab
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Open your agent in Copilot Studio, select the Build tab, and then select Tools in the components panel.
To use a published server, select Add tool, select the MCP tab, select a server, review its description and Docs link, and select Add. If prompted, enter the connection values and select Create.
To add a custom server, select Add next to the search bar in the Add a tool dialog, and then select Model Context Protocol (MCP).
On the Add MCP server page, enter a Name, a Description, the Server URL, and the Authentication details the server requires.
Select Add, review the tools that appear and their descriptions, and then select Save.
Select the Preview tab, ask a question that needs one of the server tools, and use the activity trace to confirm which tool ran, with which arguments, and what it returned.
instructions: Open your agent, select the Build tab, and then select Tools.
In the Add a tool dialog, select the MCP tab.
Capture the list of published servers, or the Add MCP server page if you add a custom server.

shots.caption: The Add hook page with an event type chosen
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Open the agent and, on the top menu bar, select the three dots (…), and then select Hooks.
In the Hooks dialog, select Create.
On the Add hook page, choose the Event type, such as Pre tool use, and enter a Name.
For a tool event, use the Tools field to select the tools the hook applies to, or leave it empty for All tools.

Select an existing published Workflow, or select New workflow. The starter workflow already has a When an agent calls the flow node and a Respond to the agent node, so keep their input and output names, add your nodes between them, then select Save and Publish.
Select Done, select the Save icon on the top menu bar to save the agent, and then publish the agent so the hook runs for users.
On the Preview tab, trigger the event, such as a tool call, and use the activity trace to confirm the hook changed or recorded what you expected.
instructions: Open the agent. On the top menu bar, select the three dots (…), and then select Hooks.
In the Hooks dialog, select Create.
Capture the Add hook page with the Event type, Name, and Tools fields visible.

shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: In the agent configuration panel on the Build tab, select Tools.
In the Add a tool dialog, select Add next to the search bar, and then select Workflow.
In the workflow designer, make sure the workflow has a When an agent calls the flow node and a Respond to the agent node, and add nodes between them to retrieve data or run business logic.
Select the Save icon in the upper-right corner, and then select Publish.
Go back to the agent's Build tab and confirm the workflow appears in the Tools list. It also appears on the Workflows page for other agents to use.
Select the Preview tab, ask a question that should trigger the workflow, and use the activity trace to verify the tool, its arguments, and its result.

Capture the designer with When an agent calls the flow and Respond to the agent visible.

shots.featureName: Triggers and autonomous agents (Microsoft Copilot harness)
shots.caption: The Triggers page with a trigger configured
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Build tab.
setup: Open the agent in Copilot Studio and select Triggers.
Select the trigger you want, such as New email.
Configure the connection until you see the green checkmark, optionally add extra instructions for this trigger, and set the Trigger options that decide when the agent runs.
If you plan to share the agent, turn Editable by user on or off for each trigger option, and expand Advanced parameters if you need them. Then select Add trigger.
Select the testing flask button, select Start listening, and create a matching event, such as sending an email. You can also choose a previous event from Test with previous trigger events.
Select Publish, and in the success dialog choose Activate for myself or Share with others.
If you chose Activate for myself, turn the agent on in Agent management.
instructions: Open the agent in Copilot Studio and select Triggers.
Select a trigger, such as New email, and configure the connection until the green checkmark appears.
Capture the page with the Trigger options and Add trigger visible.

shots.featureName: Preview and test an agent (Microsoft Copilot harness)
shots.caption: The Preview tab with a response and its activity trace
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to the Preview tab.
setup: Open the agent in Copilot Studio and select the Preview tab.
Select one of the prompt suggestions, or enter a message, and send it. The suggestions come from the agent's configuration.
Review the response, and open the activity trace to see the knowledge sources consulted, the tools invoked, and the reasoning steps.
Select a source or tool chip in the trace to jump to that component on the Build tab.
Rate a response with thumbs up or thumbs down, and add written feedback if you want.
Turn the End user preview toggle on to see the agent as end users see it, and turn it off to return to the maker view.
Note the running estimated Copilot Credits total in the Preview chat after the test conversation.
Open the conversation history and filter it by status, such as Failed or Completed, to review earlier test conversations.
instructions: Open the agent and select the Preview tab.
Send a prompt that makes the agent use knowledge or a tool.
Open the activity trace for the response and capture the Preview tab with the trace and the End user preview toggle visible.

callouts.label: Preview tab
callouts.note: Chat with the agent as you build it.

callouts.label: End user preview
callouts.note: Switches between maker view and end user view.

shots.caption: The Evaluate tab with a finished evaluation
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to Evaluate.
prerequisites: Preview and test an agent (Microsoft Copilot harness)
setup: Open the agent and select the Evaluate tab.
Start a new evaluation and add test conversations by writing them, generating them with AI, or uploading a CSV file.
Name the evaluation, select the General quality test method, and choose the agent version.
Select Evaluate to run it, and wait for the results.
Review the scores and the per-test-case credit usage to find weak spots.
Adjust the agent's instructions, knowledge, or tools, and run the evaluation again to measure the effect.
instructions: Open the agent and select the Evaluate tab.
Run an evaluation that uses the General quality test method and wait for the results.

setup: Open the agent, run a test conversation on the Preview tab, and note the running estimated Copilot Credits shown in the chat.
Open the agent's Monitor page and review the total Copilot Credits it consumed and, where shown, the breakdown by activity or outcome.
Use the Copilot Credits estimator linked from the Overview of usage-based billing article to estimate consumption for your scenario.
As an admin, open the Power Platform admin center and go to Licensing > Copilot Studio to view consumption across an environment or your tenant.
In the Power Platform admin center, go to Manage > Copilot Studio and filter the Harness column. Learn currently labels the Microsoft Copilot harness value GitHub Copilot in that column.
Review the cost controls: set environment credit allocations (prepaid capacity only), set agent limits, and disable draw from the tenant pool at scale for environments that should not overconsume.

Open the agent's Monitor page.

shots.caption: Show Work IQ configured under Tools on the agent, with connection and credential details masked.
shots.navHint: Open your agent, then go to Tools.
setup: Sign in to Copilot Studio and open an agent that uses the Microsoft Copilot harness.
On the Build tab, under Tools, select Work IQ. If the agent does not have Work IQ, add it as a tool first.
In the Edit tool dialog, review the Connection. If you need a new connection, open the connection dropdown, select Create New Connection, select Create, and complete the sign-in.
Under Sources, clear the workloads the agent doesn't need. Workloads include SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook mail, Teams, Calendar, and People, and you can select only whole workloads.
Select Done.

Optional: to use a preview workload, select the ellipsis (...) in the agent designer toolbar, select Settings, select Work IQ, turn on Enable preview workloads under Preview workloads, and select Done. Then reopen Work IQ and review Business apps (preview) under Sources.
Test the agent with a prompt that uses a selected workload, such as "Summarize my unread emails from today." and select Allow when prompted to let Work IQ connect and use services.
instructions: Show Work IQ configured under Tools on the agent, with connection and credential details masked.

callouts.label: Tools
callouts.note: Show Work IQ configured under Tools on the agent, with connection and credential details masked.

In the components panel, use the Memory toggle to turn the feature on.
On the Preview tab, tell the agent a preference, such as how you like summaries formatted, and then start a new conversation.
In the new conversation, ask for a summary and check whether the agent applies the remembered preference.
Ask the agent in chat what it remembers about you, update or forget one memory in chat, and open the memory portal link the agent shows to View memories.

In the components panel, turn the Memory toggle on.
